findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed the raw steak stored over raw fish, and raw ground pork stored over cooked baked potatoes. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and moved the fish above the the steak and to the side so that fish was not stored below steak, and the ground pork was moved to a lower shelf where it was below raw whole steak and above raw chicken. Ensure that foods are stored properly in order of final cooking temperatures: RTE foods and washed produced (no cooking) on top, followed by unwashed produce, followed by eggs (135 F), then fish (135 F), then whole intact meat (145 F), ground and comminuted meat (155 F), and finally chicken and poultry (165 F) on the bottom shelf.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed that the hot box in the kitchen was not hot holding recently cooked food at 135 F and above: marinara was probed at 130 F and green beans were probed at 125 F. CORRECTED: PIC took all containers back to the oven and stove to reheat them above 165 F and determined that the hot box needed to be turned up higher. Temperatures were remeasured at 151 F (marinara) and 153 F (green beans) and the ambient air temperature of the hot box was measurably hot. Ensure that cooked food items are hot held at internal temperatures of 135 F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that a spray bottle with degreaser solution was unlabeled. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the spray bottle was labeled immediately. Ensure that all chemicals that are in working containers be labeled to prevent food or surface contamination or improper use.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed several single-use containers and single-service articles stored upright where the food-contact surfaces were exposed to contamination from falling debris. CORRECTED: PIC had all items either inverted or placed under a shelf where they would be protected. Ensure all single-service and single-use articles and utensils are protected from contamination during storage, either through a protective container, inversion, or an upper barrier.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed the underside of the shelf above the steam table has accumulated debris from old food splashes. The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean it later and add it to the regular cleaning schedule. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are maintained clean of food residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Dented cans were observed in dry storage. The observed cans were shown and discussed with the PIC. The cans were removed for discard to correct. Insure package integrity of all cans in the facility moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: (1) A dirty knife was observed with food debris on the magnetic rack next to the three part sink. (2) A food dicer tool was observed with remaining food debris while stored on top of the ice machine. The PIC was notified and shown both items, and they were moved back to dish to correct. Insure that all food-contact items are completely clean prior to storage to sight and touch at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: A spray bottle with degreaser solution was unlabeled. It is important that all chemicals that are in working containers be labeled to prevent cross contamination or improper use. The PIC was notified and the spray bottle was labeled immediately.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Personal items were stored in a metal cooking pan along with a stem thermometer. PIC was shown and the thermometer was washed to correct. Food contact utensils should be stored so that they are not exposed to sources of contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(1) and A(3)-(8) Prohibitions. (A) Cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (8) Under other sources of contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The underside of the shelf above the steam table was observed to have accumulated debris from old food splashes. The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean it later at the end of the day, and clean it on a regular schedule. It is important that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are maintained clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee was preparing a wrap for a customer using their bare hands. The employee was educated and they washed hands and put on gloves to continue preparing foods. The PIC will be reminding all staff about proper food handling. Ensure that employees always handle ready-to-eat foods with gloves or another barrier.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The caulking to the right of the dish machine is starting to degrade; the caulking must be repaired/replaced to seal the surface to the wall. 

(2) The gasket on the left door of the cookline freezer is not fully attached; the gasket must be repaired/replaced. 

Ensure that the above referenced are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the salad prep cooler has an accumulation of food residue on the bottom. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the bottom of the salad prep cooler is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated on the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: A half consumed water bottle is observed in the kitchen on a lower shelf next to closed a plastic tub holding clean wrapped utensils. Containers for employees to drink out of should have lids and straws. Designating a storage area away from food and clean utensil storage is optimal. The bottle was discarded in the garbage.

(A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Inspector observed the floor wall juncture to be soiled in the kitchen. Take care to clean the heavily soiled areas and maintain them clean by sweeping all the way to the wall before mopping. The facility has purchased a small pressure washer to help with this build up. Take care not to shove water under the walls with the pressure washer. Clean and maintain these areas clean especially the area under the dish area and the area to the left of the hand sink on the cook line. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an employee check their text messages on their watch with gloved hands and then proceed to return to cooking on the grill and food prep. The employee was stopped and coached on correct times to wash hands and proper glove use. The violation is considered corrected at time of inspection. Take every opportunity to coach proper hand washing.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the base cabinets at the server station to be soiled with soda splash on the outside and leaking soda boxes on the inside. The material is raw wood and is no longer smooth, and nonabsorbent. Repair or replace the base cabinets to meat the requirements of this part. 

4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

Observed employee grab a piece of fried mushroom and eat it while behind the cook line. The order of mushrooms was a mistake and he was eating them. The employee was coached immediately on the proper use of single use gloves and eating or drinking while preparing food. Employee left the prep line with the mushrooms. The violation is considered corrected.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Au gratin potatoes are observed on the hot line at 102F. The facility put the food into the oven to reheat to 165F. The potatoes had been hot holding for approximately 3 hours.  The potatoes were also double panned in the hot well. Make sure to single pan the potatoes or use a deeper pan. The violation is considered corrected. Evaluate the hot line with a probe thermometer regularly.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Observed floors under the bar at the corner with exposed pipes soiled. Also floor under the 3 part sink in the kitchen is also soiled. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

Observed the  shelf above mixer to have personal belongings stored on it. Items were removed. The violation is considered corrected. The items may be stored there if they are stored in a solid container. Store items properly so that they do not pose potential contamination risk to clean items.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Salisbury steak placed in the hot holding well at approximately 1:45pm temped out at 119F approximately 45 minutes later. The food was taken off of the line and placed into the oven. The meat portions were heated to 174F internally. The food is currently holding at 144F. Make sure to get food up to appropriate holding temperature before putting on the hot holding line. The individual steaks come in pre cooked frozen and are placed on a sheet pan to be heated in the oven.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Chicken portions in the make table are 55F. The chicken was cooked, cut, portioned and placed into the top of the unit at approximately 1:45pm according to management. Make sure that the chicken is completely cooled before it is placed into the prep top to hold. The chicken portions were moved to a sheet pan and placed into the walk in freezer to cool completely.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Observed walls under the 3 part sink in the kitchen, behind the cook line, under the dish machine, and behind the hanging rack above the salad prep cooler to be soiled with food splash. The floors in these same areas along with floors under the bar at the corner with exposed pipes are also soiled. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed multiple employee’s to improperly wash hands. Ensure hands are washed with warm water and soap for at least 20 seconds, paper towels are used to dry hands, and faucets are turned off with a barrier such as the used paper towel - prevent cross contamination of hands. No barrier was used multiple times. Discussed with employee’s and PIC. Ensure proper hand washing is reviewed and staff is aware of the barrier method to turn off the faucets after appropriate hand washing. COS.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed the steak cold holding drawer (below the grill on the prep line) to be out of temperature. Two types of steaks were probed with a thermometer - 52 degrees F and 48 degrees F. Some steaks were still partially frozen. Inspector asked one of the cooks how long the steaks had been in the cold holding drawer. He stated they were prepped earlier before lunch. Inspector instructed employees to put the steaks in the walk-in cooler and ice for rapid cooling. Discussed where steaks will be held while the cooler is down. PIC stated either an ice bath method will be used on the prep surfaces during dinner/lunch rushes and/or employee’s will go back and forth to the walk-in cooler as needed for steaks. Both methods will suffice until the drawer cooler is fixed. Bormida was called to service the cooler drawer. Drawer historically has troubles holding temperatures below 41 degrees F. It is an older piece of equipment. PIC stated owner has discussed replacing this particular piece of equipment due to age and issues holding temperature accurately. Inspector will follow-up on 7/25/22.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the gasket/seal of the walk-in cooler to be coming away from the door. Discussed with PIC. The walk-in freezer gasket/seal has been ordered and is in the process of being fixed. Walk-in freezer gasket/seal was an issue during the last inspection. Ensure both areas are repaired before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the walk-in freezer fan to have an accumulation of dust. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 11/4/21 and 2/15/22.

Observed the walk-in cooler to have a mild accumulation of dust. Observed the back wall of the prep area near the grill (under the microwave shelf) to have food splash and debris. The areas behind the fryers have grease debris behind them, as well. Ensure routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple areas of the facility to have stacks of cup that were wet. Cups should be air dried before being stacked. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 11/4/21. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed gasket/seal to be coming away from the walk-in freezer. Repair the seal/gasket before the next routine inspection. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the fans of the walk-in freezer to have an accumulation of dust. Ensure routine cleaning of the fans within coolers. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 11/4/21.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 

Observed stacks of cups at the waiter server area that are being stacked wet and not air drying before stacking. Discussed practice with PIC. Ensure proper air drying of cups before stacking in this area or any other area of the facility.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the fans of the walk-in freezer to have an accumulation of dust. Ensure routine cleaning of the fans within coolers.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Discussed document with PIC. Provided copy for facility. Ensure all employee’s understand importance and details of document and sign. Ensure new hires review and sign. Inspector will follow-up on 6/28/21.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee to wash hands near kitchen hand sink by dish machine and not turn off faucet handles with barrier. Discussed with PIC. Proper hand washing requires washing hands with soap and water for 15-20 seconds, followed by turning off faucet with a barrier such as paper towels. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact areas to not be clean:
1. Soda nozzle holder at the bar had accumulation of mold. Discussed with bartender. Bartender washed, rinsed, and sanitized soda nozzle holder on site. COS.
2. Ice scoop was resting above ice machine and not on a surface that could be easily cleaned - washed, rinsed, and sanitized. PIC took ice scoop to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized and provided a metal sheet tray for the ice scoop to rest on top of during hours of operation. Wash, rinse, and sanitize both tray and scoop frequently.

Discussed routine cleaning of food-contact surfaces with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple areas of the facility to have single-service items to be upright and food- and lip-contact areas to be exposed to cross contamination. Items were inverted during inspection. Discussed proper storage with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed several areas of to be in need of caulking: hand sink near fry grills and dish machine. Sink and dish machine are coming away from wall and need caulked. Repair before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

(REPEAT) Observed mop to be stored in a manner that does not allow to air and/or drip dry. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/9/20.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14  (P) Employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

Observed employee to greet and help inspector then proceeed to return to cook line for order without washing hands before donning single-use gloves. Hands should be washed between changing tasks. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 100 ppm in several sanitization buckets. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed several buckets of sanitiziter to be low on concentration, 100 ppm. Discussed routine changing of sanitization solution in order to maintain a concentration of 200 to 400 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13  (C) Frozen fish is thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Packaging must be removed from fish in ROP prior to thawing under refrigeration or running water. Reference 3-501.13.

Observed multiple pieces of salmon to be thawed within the reduced oxygen packaging. Discussed either cutting open packaging before thawing or removing from packaging and places in shallow trays with a cover. This is a repeat violation since the previous inspection in 2019.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop to be stored incorrectly in-between uses. Mops should be hung in a manner that allows to drip dry and/or air dry. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC. COS.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Observed staff touch ready-to-eat sandwich with bare hands while holding to cut sandwich in half with a knife. Discussed the importance of preventing bare hand contact with ready to eat foods to prevent the spread of illness. 

->Food employee used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods. Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. Reference 3-301.11.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Hand washing sink behind the bar was not provided with hand towels at the time of inspection. Hand sink was restocked during inspection. 

->Disposable paper towels not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide disposable paper towels, hand soap, and hot and cold water at hand washing sinks to facilitate proper hand washing practices. Reference 6-301.12.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
Pan of pulled pork measured at 66F in the upright hot holding cabinet. Staff indicated items were reheated in the oven and transferred to hot holding cabinet just prior to inspection.

->Food must be reheated to 165°F within 2 hours, before being placed in hot holding. Reviewed reheating requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Food was reheated to 165F in the oven. Reference 3-403.11.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Baked potatoes measured at 56F on pan on a speed rack in the walk-in cooler. Pan of ribs measured at 46F-53F on pan on a speed rack in the walk-in cooler. Pans were noted stored closely together. Staff indicated items were cooked the night prior, estimated around 9 pm. Staff indicated items had been in the walk-in cooler all night and day. Items were discarded. 

->Discussed allowing space between pans of cooling items to allow adequate air flow to assist the cooling process. 

->Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.14.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Salmon found completely thawed in ROP vacuum sealed packages in the bottom pull-out drawer cooler across from the stove top. Discussed introducing air into vacuum sealed packages for proper thawing practices.

->Frozen fish is thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Packaging must be removed from fish in ROP prior to thawing under refrigeration or running water. Reference 3-501.13.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Door gasket on the bottom pull out drawer found in disrepair and pulled away from the door (also heavily soiled) located in the 2 door pull-out cold holding unit across from the stove top.

->Replace the damaged or missing gaskets so the cooler can hold food at the proper temperature. Reference 4-501.11.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed moldy caulk at the dish sink. Replace or clean the caulk to remove the mold.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment:
Observed an employee handle raw hamburger and switch tasks (handle buns). This is not a proper practice. Wash hands any time they may have been contaminated or switching tasks.
750-160(a) Food shall be prepared with the least possible manual contact, using suitable utensils and using surfaces that have been cleaned, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent cross-contamination.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed a soiled apron stored above potatoes that are prepped to be baked. This is not a proper practice. Prevent potential cross contamination.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed orange juice with no date mark. Date mark product and use within seven days or provide information to prove it is not potentially hazardous.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a cracked spatula on the rack ready for use. The spatula was discarded during the inspection.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) (REPEAT) Observed the floor in the dish area needs repaired (coving). 2) Observed the kitchen floor needing repainted in the dish area and the cookline. Repaint or seal the floor to make it a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed cheese sauce cooling with no time mark. The cheese sauce was in the walk in freezer and time was marked on the sheet to ensure proper cooling of the product. Anytime facility is cooling food it must be time marked to ensure proper cooling.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed fettuccine Alfredo sauce that was past the seven days. The sauce was discarded during the inspection. All potentially hazardous foods must used or discarded within seven days.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed corn beef improperly thawing in the three compartment sink. There are four proper ways to thaw. The beef was moved to the walk in cooler.
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed cheese sauce cooling in the walk in freezer was stored on the ground. The food must be at least 6" off the floor. Provide proper protection of the food.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed four-five food utensils with cracks. These are not smooth and easily cleanable products. Owner stated they will be discarded and replaced.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the can opener blade to be soiled. Clean the food contact surfaces after use.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the fan in the dish area to be dusty. Clean the non- food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor in the dish area needs repaired due to construction and it also needs repainted. Seal the floor and the coving.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed raw fish stored above ready to eat green beans. The fish was moved to a lower shelf. Make sure to properly store food to prevent cross contamination.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed wet wiping cloths stored on the counters. Cloths were submerged in a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Make sure to properly store all wet wiping cloths in sanitizer.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed pans stored under the potatoes charred with heavy debris builduip. 2) Observed the knife racks where clean knives are stored to be soiled. Clean the food contact surfaces.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the top of the dish machine to be soiled with debris. Clean the non-food contact surface.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed beverage napkins stored on the floor in the bar area. The napkins were moved to be stored at least 6" off the floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
Observed a blocked handwashing sink at the bar. The handsink was made accessible during the inspection, make sure all handwashing sinks are accessible at all times.
750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floors underneath the fryers to be soiled. Clean the floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment: The food on the steam table is 120F. The hot table was turned up and more water added to the table. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) Foods were reheated to 170F.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: The cook took the bun off the grill with a spatula and then touched it with his bare hands to arrange it on the prep surface. 750-160 Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.  The bun was discarded and the cook placed a glove on one hand for handling ready to eat foods.  Utilize a glove or other clean barrier for contact with ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed the body of the ice scoop to have a large crack in it. 750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleansable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices. Replace ice scoop.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: Observed wet wiping cloths to be sitting on the prep surfaces. Bucket for these cloths has 100ppm of quat sanitizer.  Also hanging bucket of sanitizer has 0ppm of sanitizer available. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. The buckets were refreshed. Store cloths in sanitizer as required.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The drop guard of the ice machine is soiled.  750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use and any time they may have become contaminated.  The drop guard was pulled and placed through the ice machine.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: The floor under the dish machine is soiled especially between the leg of the machine and the wall. Also, the floor between the rack and the ice machine has some litter.  750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors and maintain clean.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Taco meat on the counter cooling does not have time on the label. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Place time labels along with date for cooling potentially hazardous foods.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Foods in the prep top are above 41F including 7 chicken portions at 45, 7 hard cooked eggs 4 turkey portions and 2 ham portions. 750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service. Foods were discarded in the garbage and ice was added to the top.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: Taco meat on the counter at 98F and 100F. Meat had been cooling on the counter for 30 minutes according to staff. 750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours. The meat was placed into the walk in freezer and reached 70F before 2 hours had passed. The was stirred and placed back into the walk in freezer to continue to cool.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: The  facility had several wiping cloths sitting on prep counters. Also the sanitizer bucket in the kitchen had less than 200ppm of quat in it. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The following food contact surfaces are soiled: 1) ice machine drop guard. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. Drop guard was cleaned.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The following non food contact surfaces are soiled 1) fan covers in walk in cooler 2) shelf with chemicals 3) around grill tops 4) radio top 5) bottom of meat cooler with water 6) front of the wait station cabinets. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: The floors in the following areas are soiled 1) floor sinks at the 3 part and at the dish area 20 floor under tea at the wait station. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors and maintain clean.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: BBQ sauce prepared in house is sitting on the table cooling with no date or time. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Provide date and time on foods that are cooling. Sauce was placed on an ice bath and then into the freezer to cool. Sauce was 68F in one hour.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: Dish machine has an accumulation of lime and some soil. 750-830i All dish washing machines shall be thoroughly cleaned at least once a day or more often when necessary to maintain them in satisfactory operating condition. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: Observed wet wiping cloths on the shelf and back of sink during inspection. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. Store cloths in sanitizer between uses.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Floor sinks in the kitchen and area under the dish machine is soiled. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors and maintain clean.
